cells.tense: You are here at the table with your pen, and the mix holds.
cells.act: hand one thing on in the way you were handed it
cells.ask: Take something that was taught to you and pass it along exactly as it reached you — same words, same order — some time in the next few weeks.
cells.core:
The reason you can stand in a complicated moment without going blank is that the pieces are genuinely in there together — the hard parts and the light ones both. When something shifts, you adjust, and the adjustment comes from having everything in one place. People leave a conversation with you feeling met where they were.

What this balance is free to feed next is the passing-on. Some time in the next few weeks, take one thing that was taught to you and give it to someone else the way it reached you — same words, same order, without fitting it to them mid-sentence. What gets handed on whole is what stays alive between people. Which parts of it you actually believe is something you'll find out when you hear yourself say them.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold what's messy and still find the note.
cells.verb: sensing the moment and giving it exactly what it needs
cells.place: the point where everything gathered arrives and lets go at once

cells.tense: You are bracing for a harmony that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.act: go where the feeling is already pulling
cells.ask: For a week, go where your own feeling is already pulling instead of waiting for the agreeable moment — and say what you're doing to whoever it touches.
cells.core:
When a disagreement gets smoothed over before anyone has objected, the blend comes early. Differences get rounded off, the talk stays pleasant, and nothing gets settled. The adjusting itself is fine — it's just running past what it's meant to serve, with no pull in it, only a shape of agreement nobody has weighed.

For a week, go where your own feeling is already pulling, rather than waiting for the moment that keeps things agreeable. Let the people it touches know what you're doing; a difference out in the open can sit at a table without the table going to pieces. Direction keeps any harmony true. The pleasant version would have you wait for the right moment — this is the moment.
cells.sheetLine: Smoothing it early keeps the tune and loses the point.

cells.tense: You were at the door of it once, and you're still standing there.
cells.act: stay in contact while it is hard
cells.ask: Stay with one person through something hard for ten minutes without steering it, then close honestly and leave the rest where it is.
cells.core:
What comes in goes back out the same afternoon. Nothing has time to settle, so each conversation lands and scatters before it can join the last one. The knack for blending is still there; it just has nothing gathered to work with, and every new thing finds nothing waiting and starts from scratch.

Company fills that, not effort. Stay with one person who is in something hard for ten minutes without steering it, close the conversation honestly when it ends, and leave the rest of what you carry where it is. The centre comes back the same way — by staying inside one thing long enough that it's allowed to matter. Ten minutes of staying is the whole assignment; longer is not required.

cells.tense: Your pen is down, and the page is already filling.
cells.act: teach it the way it was taught to you, with one change
cells.ask: One older person knows a way you're already using without having learned it — ask them how they do it, then try it their way once, with one thing changed.
cells.core:
You adjust and blend without noticing the moving parts, so it doesn't get counted as work. The balance happens, and afterwards it looks like nothing happened at all. Some of that is you shaping the mix; some of it is the people who did this before you, whose way you're using without having looked at it.

There's someone older who knows a way you're already using — ask them how they do it. Then try it their way once, with one thing changed by you. Following an older way closely, once, is how your own way gets made in the open: you'll feel where you're building on it and where you're departing, instead of doing both in the dark.
cells.sheetLine: You've been blending. You can't yet say what.
